reviews.reasons: NO_PLAN is the right stance. The only opening (cop_e73492ae9f1441edb0ca) has six WRITTEN_ACCEPTANCE agreements at $1,500 = $9,000, but every agreement's deliverable states net 45 from an invoice issued on delivery day 3, so the earliest settlement is day 48 against a 14-day window: $0 settles in time. This is a genuine constraint, not missing evidence: even with every buyer and every fact established, the signed terms put the cash outside the window. Recomputed: 4 x $1,500 = $6,000 >= $5,000 (3 x $1,500 = $4,500 would fall short), so the stated resolution (4 signers agreeing in writing to pay on delivery, or a deadline >= 48 days) is arithmetically right. Engineer cost $600/stamp invoiced net 60 means no up-front capital, consistent with exposure cap 0. Decisive link SETTLES_IN_TIME matches Brain's own link check (48 days vs 14) and the DEADLINE constraint cites the card's timeToFirstCash and price fields.
findings: Decisive gap correctly named: SETTLES_IN_TIME, basis card timeToFirstCash = 48 days and each agreement's net-45 term.
Arithmetic verified: 6 x $1,500 = $9,000 at day 48; 0 in window; resolution threshold of 4 pay-on-delivery signers is the minimum that clears $5,000.
Minor: the alternatives do not mention invoice factoring/early-payment discount as a route to in-window cash; no evidence on the card supports one, so it does not change the stance.
The RESEARCH step (asking the six signers for pay-on-delivery terms) is the correct next test and takes no orders before fulfilment is shown possible (Ridgeway PE quote on card).
